beats.text: At the start of the 1900s, two events four months apart changed Texas forever.
On September the 8th, 1900, a hurricane struck the city of Galveston,
then the biggest port in Texas.
Somewhere between 6,000 and 12,000 people died.
It is still the deadliest natural disaster in American history.
Then on January the 10th, 1901, near Beaumont, a well at a hill called
Spindletop blew oil *150* feet into the sky.
The Texas oil boom had begun, and money started pouring into a
city nearby, one that would grow to replace Galveston, *Houston*.
Back to the Dial.
It is still locked on blue, but how do you keep one party
in power for a whole century?
Part of the answer is simple.
For generations of white Texans, voting Republican meant voting for the party
of the Union Army and Reconstruction.
It just wasn't *done*.
The other part is about who was allowed to vote.
In 1902, Texas added a *poll tax*.
You had to pay to vote.
It hit poor voters of every race, and especially Black and Mexican American Texans.
Then came the white primary.
The Democratic Party simply barred Black voters from its primaries,
and since the Democrats always won in November, the primary was the
only election that mattered.
A Black dentist from Houston named Lonnie Smith took that system
all the way to the Supreme Court.
In 1944, in *Smith v. Allwright*, the court struck down the white
primary, eight votes to one.
The lawyer who argued his case was a young Thurgood *Marshall*.
Now, here's the *twist* that sets up everything that comes next.
Inside that one giant Democratic Party, Texans still argued.
There were liberal Democrats and conservative Democrats, and they fought
each other fiercely in the primaries.
For decades, the conservative wing usually won, which meant that in
practice, Texas was a conservative state that voted *Democrat*.
And that is stage one of the one-party *trap* I promised you.
When the primary is the only election that matters, the real fight moves
inside the party, and the party *splits*.
Keep that in mind, because the moment those conservative Democrats found a
new home, the Dial was going to move.
Two more stages to go.
